assertions.description: window.isSecureContext is exposed as a boolean — the page-observable signal Ask-before-HTTP steers toward.
A page delivered over https: is a secure context (vacuously true when this suite runs on a non-https page).
An http: page on loopback (localhost / 127.0.0.1 / [::1]) is still a secure context — the reason Balanced mode never warns on local development (vacuously true off loopback).
assertions.test: (() => { const h = location.hostname; const loop = h === 'localhost' || h.endsWith('.localhost') || h === '127.0.0.1' || h === '[::1]'; return !(location.protocol === 'http:' && loop) || window.isSecureContext === true; })()

assertions.description: A plaintext http: page on a non-loopback host must NOT be a secure context — the state the Chrome 154 warning asks about (vacuously true when this suite runs elsewhere).
assertions.test: (() => { const h = location.hostname; const loop = h === 'localhost' || h.endsWith('.localhost') || h === '127.0.0.1' || h === '[::1]'; return !(location.protocol === 'http:' && !loop) || window.isSecureContext === false; })()

assertions.description: Navigating to a public HTTP-only site in Chrome 154+ shows the full-page 'doesn't support a secure connection' warning before any plaintext request is sent.
assertions.test: The interstitial is pre-navigation browser UI with no DOM, event, or API surface a page can observe or dispatch. Verify manually: Chrome 154+ (or chrome://flags/#https-first-balanced-mode on older channels), navigate to an HTTP-only public site, observe the warning; Continue-to-site is remembered per host.

assertions.description: The HttpsOnlyMode enterprise policy (allowed / disallowed / force_enabled / force_balanced_enabled) controls the mode, and HttpAllowlist exempts named hosts.
assertions.test: Policy behaviour requires a managed browser: set HttpsOnlyMode via chrome://policy on a managed profile and observe the Always Use Secure Connections setting lock in chrome://settings/security. Not observable from page script.
